title: Tenant FastBoot Preloader and KV Hydrator for Cold-start Reduction
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective:
Reduce cold-start P95/P99 latency for Dedicated tenants by preloading model weights and priming KV cache while preserving throughput guarantees and not interfering with live inference traffic. This ticket scopes the FastBoot Preloader and KV Hydrator: a tenant-aware background orchestrator that performs staged weight slices loading and lightweight KV probing prior to request spikes.

Background:
Customers on Dedicated report periodic cold-start spikes when new model versions or tenant weight slices are pulled into GPU memory. Current warm pools reduce some of this, but we see residual P99 increases when bursts land on cold shards or when KV caches are empty. We need a predictable, admission-controlled preloader that: 1) respects reserved throughput commitments, 2) limits prefetch overhead during high load, and 3) provides clear telemetry for cost attribution.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce observed cold-start P99 latency by >= 50% for targeted tenants in canary (internal) benchmarks.
- No more than 3% sustained increase in GPU cycles used for background preloads during steady-state traffic.
- Safe rollout path: feature off by default, opt-in per-tenant flag, canary to 10 tenants before wide release.

Scope in this ticket:
- Design and implement the FastBoot Preloader service (scheduler + worker) that runs in the Dedicated control plane and issues prioritized preload jobs to node agents.
- Implement KV Hydrator: targeted prefix probes and limited-size synthetic inference to populate KV caches without executing full expensive token generation.
- Admission controls and backpressure hooks into the runtime to ensure preloads yield to live request SLOs.
- Metrics/alerts and trace propagation for visibility and cost accounting.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does NOT implement cross-tenant weight eviction policies or billing changes. Those are follow-ups.

High-level design summary:
- Tenant FastBoot Preloader: receives signals (scheduled ramp, tenant traffic forecast, commit to new model version, or explicit API trigger). It computes a prioritized preload plan consisting of weight-slices and KV probe tasks. Prioritization uses tenant tier, SLA, recent traffic delta, and model hotness score.
- Staged preload lanes: critical (core layers and embeddings), bulk (remaining weight slices), and background (non-critical tensors and optional optimizer state). Each lane has configurable concurrency, bandwidth caps, and soft time budgets.
- KV Hydrator: for each tenant, sampler builds a short list of high-value prefixes (from recent request samples or provided prompt-set) and dispatches small-range prefix queries to the runtime to populate KV cache and attention key/value stores. Probes are low-latency synthetic calls with controlled token length and per-tenant rate limits.
- Admission control & safety: node-agent exposes a preload QoS API with three signals: current_inflight_load, token_emission_rate, and available_gpu_headroom. Preloader uses these to throttle or pause lanes. Preloads also respect reserved capacity markers for Dedicated tenants so they do not cannibalize on-demand pools.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) PoC scheduler + single-node worker that can request weight slice loads and run a synthetic KV probe (2 sprints).
2) Node-agent preload QoS API and runtime integration hooks (patches to loader and KV layer) (1 sprint).
3) Prioritization rules, admission policy DSL, and tenant opt-in config (1 sprint).
4) Telemetry, cost accounting tags, and runbook + canary (1 sprint).

Telemetry and success metrics:
- Per-tenant cold-start P50/P95/P99 before/after comparing identical spike traces.
- Preload CPU/GPU seconds per tenant per hour.
- Number of blocked/throttled preload attempts due to QoS.
- KV hit-rate delta after hydrator runs.
- Cost delta on sample tenants.

Rollout and canary strategy:
- Feature gated by tenant flag. Initial internal canary (3 internal tenants), then opt-in by engineering partners (10 tenants), then staged escalation. Each stage: 72-hour observation window and rollback triggers on P99 regressions or >5% sustained GPU overhead.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/17530981/FastBoot+Preloader+and+KV+Hydrator
- Prototype dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.io/d/fastboot/preload-summary
- Runtime PR (node-agent hooks): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4587
- Control plane scheduler PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/221

Notes on cost/accounting:
Preloads will be tagged with tenant and preload_lane metadata so usage and cost can be broken out in Console. We need pricing/product input for whether background preloads are billed at a discounted rate or attributed to reserved capacity.

Open questions:
- Should hydrator probes be replayed with a small sampling of user prompt-sets vs. synthetic prompts? (security and data retention concerns)
- What is the correct soft-limit for background GPU usage in low-latency SLO tenants?
- Should we allow cross-tenant collateral preloads when GPUs have large contiguous headroom?

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Preloads compete with live traffic and cause SLO regression. Mitigation: strict admission control and initial low-concurrency lanes in canary.
- Risk: KV probes could leak or access PII if synthetic prompts are constructed poorly. Mitigation: force opt-in, sanitize prefix sources, and enforce no-logging for probe payloads.
- Risk: Weight-slice ordering mistakes could leave user-critical layers unloaded. Mitigation: critical-lane tests and acceptance criteria below.
acceptance_criteria: Canary tenants (internal) show >=50% improvement in cold-start P99 on synthetic spike tests
Preloader respects node-agent QoS signals and will pause when available_gpu_headroom < configured_threshold
KV Hydrator increases per-tenant KV hit rate by at least 25% in 10 minutes after hydrator run in benchmark traces
All preload jobs emitted include tenant and lane tags and appear in Console cost breakdown
Feature is behind tenant-level opt-in flag and can be disabled remotely without component restarts
rollout_plan: Deploy scheduler and node-agent hooks to canary cluster (internal)
Enable feature for 3 internal tenants, monitor 72 hours
Expand to 10 opt-in customers with engineering support
If stable, promote config to dedicated runtime release channel and include feature note in runtime-2.3 release
